summary: Couch Investor's Neil hosts a head-to-head debate with his former live-stream co-host Jose (described as 'the number one Nvidia analyst on YouTube') on whether NVIDIA or Broadcom is the better AI-chip buy at current prices. Both agree both stocks look cheap: Broadcom at 20.5x forward earnings despite expected revenue growth of 65.8%/63.6%/57.2% through FY28 (toward $272B), and Nvidia at 18.7x forward with a PEG of ~0.5. Neil's key argument for Broadcom is Hock Tan's unusually concrete visibility — AI revenue doubling to $115B in FY27 and again to ~$230B the year after, guided conservatively against 30GW of visible compute demand. Jose's bull case for Nvidia is breadth: a core option on autonomous vehicles, robotics, 'data center in space', physical AI, and new neo-cloud revenue-sharing partnerships worth ~$40B in content. Both flag the mirror-image risk: customers building custom ASICs threatens Nvidia, while Anthropic/OpenAI concentration (>30% of Broadcom's two-year compute demand) threatens Broadcom. The verdict is a genuine split: Neil takes the contrarian Broadcom side for 12-month relative outperformance off the recent price divergence; Jose picks Nvidia if forced to one, sizing a both-positions split 60/40 to 65/35 in Nvidia's favor. No single explicit buy call on either name — Neil says outright he 'cannot give you a clear answer'. Other names discussed: AMD (referenced from their earlier episode), Meta (Broadcom AI-chip collaboration), TSMC (supply-chain allocation), plus Anthropic/OpenAI as key customers (both private).
title: NVIDIA vs. Broadcom: The Market Is Missing This
